verses.text: How di city sit solitary, wey dey full of people! How she don become like widow, wey dey great among di nations! She wey be princess among di provinces don become forced labourer!
She weep bitterly for di night, and her tears dey on her cheeks. Among all her lovers she get none to comfort her. All her friends don deal treacherously with her. Dem don become her enemies.
Judah don go into captivity because of affliction and hard servitude. She dwell among di nations. She find no rest. All her persecutors overtake her for di midst of narrow places.
Di roads to Zion dey mourn, because none dey come to di solemn assembly. All her gates dey desolate. Her priests sigh. Her virgins dey afflicted, and she dey bitter.
Her adversaries don become di head. Her enemies prosper, because di Lord don afflict her for di multitude of her transgressions. Her young children don go into captivity before di adversary.
From di daughter of Zion all her majesty don depart. Her princes don become like deer wey find no pasture, and dem don go without strength before di pursuer.

Jerusalem remember for di days of her affliction and of her wandering all di pleasant things wey she get from di days of old. When her people fall into di hand of di adversary, and no one help her, di adversaries see her. Dem mock at her desolations.
Jerusalem don grievously sin. Therefore she don become unclean. All wey honour her despise her, because dem don see her nakedness. Yes, she sigh, and turn backward.
Her filthiness dey for her skirts. She no remember her latter end. Therefore she come down wonderfully. She get no comforter. “Look, di Lord, at my affliction, because di enemy don triumph.”
Di adversary don spread out im hand on all her pleasant things, because she don see say di nations don enter her sanctuary, wey you command say dem no suppose enter into your assembly.
All her people sigh. Dem dey seek bread. Dem don give dem pleasant things for food to refresh di soul. “Look, di Lord, and see, because I don become despised.”
“E no mean anything to una, all una wey pass by? Look, and see if any sorrow dey like my sorrow, wey dem don do to me, wey di Lord don afflict me for di day of im fierce anger.
From on high e don send fire into my bones, and e prevail against dem. E don spread net for my feet. E don turn me back. E don make me desolate and faint all di day.

Di yoke of my transgressions dey bound by im hand. Dem dey knit together. Dem dey come up on my neck. E don make my strength fail. Di Lord don deliver me into di hands of dem wey I no fit stand against.
Di Lord don set at nothing all my mighty men for my midst. E don call solemn assembly against me to crush my young men. Di Lord don tread di virgin daughter of Judah as for di winepress.
For dis things I weep. My eye, my eye run down with water, because di comforter wey suppose relieve my soul dey far from me. My children dey desolate, because di enemy don prevail.”
Zion spread out her hands. None to comfort her. Di Lord don command concerning Jacob say im neighbours go be im adversaries. Jerusalem don become unclean thing among dem.
“Di Lord dey righteous, because I don rebel against im commandment. Hear now, all una peoples, and see my sorrow. My virgins and my young men don go into captivity.
I call for my lovers, but dem deceive me. My priests and my elders die for di city, while dem seek food for demselves to refresh dem souls.
See, di Lord, because I dey in distress. My heart dey troubled. My heart turn over inside me, because I don grievously rebel. Outside di sword bereave, inside e be like death.
Dem don hear say I sigh. None dey to comfort me. All my enemies don hear of my trouble. Dem dey glad say you don do am. You go bring di day wey you don announce, and dem go be like me.
Make all dem wickedness come before you. Do to dem as you don do to me for all my transgressions, because my sighs many, and my heart dey faint.”
How di Lord don cover di daughter of Zion with cloud for im anger! E don cast down from heaven to di earth di glory of Israel, and no remember im footstool for di day of im anger.

Di Lord don swallow up all di habitations of Jacob, and no pity. E don throw down for im wrath di strongholds of di daughter of Judah. E don bring dem down to di ground. E don profane di kingdom and im princes.
E don cut off for fierce anger all di horn of Israel. E don draw back im right hand from before di enemy. E burn against Jacob like flaming fire wey devour all round.
E don bend im bow like enemy. E don stand with im right hand like adversary, and don kill all wey dey pleasant to di eye. For di tent of di daughter of Zion e don pour out im wrath like fire.
Di Lord don become like enemy. E don swallow up Israel. E don swallow up all her palaces. E don destroy im strongholds, and don increase for di daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.

E don violently take away im tabernacle, like garden. E don destroy im place of assembly. Di Lord don cause solemn assembly and Sabbath to dey forgotten for Zion, and for im fierce anger don despise king and priest.
Di Lord don cast off im altar. E don abhor im sanctuary. E don give up into di hand of di enemy di walls of her palaces. Dem don make noise for di house of di Lord, as for day of solemn assembly.
Di Lord don purpose to destroy di wall of di daughter of Zion. E don stretch out di line. E no withdraw im hand from destroying. E don make di rampart and di wall lament. Dem languish together.
Her gates don sink into di ground. E don destroy and break her bars. Her king and her princes dey among di nations where di law no dey. Her prophets no find vision from di Lord.
Di elders of di daughter of Zion sit on di ground, dem dey silent. Dem don throw dust on dem heads. Dem don gird dem with sackcloth. Di virgins of Jerusalem hang down dem heads to di ground.

My eyes fail with tears. My heart dey troubled. My liver dey poured on di ground, because of di destruction of di daughter of my people, because di children and di infants faint for di streets of di city.
Dem talk to dem mothers, “Where grain and wine dey?” as dem faint like wounded man for di streets of di city, as dem pour out dem soul for dem mothers bosom.

Wetin I go speak as witness for you? Wetin I go liken to you, daughter of Jerusalem? Wetin I go compare to you, so that I go comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? Because your breach dey great like di sea. Who fit heal you?
Your prophets don see for you vain and foolish visions. Dem no uncover your iniquity, to restore your fortunes, but don see for you false oracles and causes of banishment.
All wey pass by clap dem hands at you. Dem hiss and shake dem heads at di daughter of Jerusalem: “Na dis be di city wey dem dey call di perfection of beauty, di joy of all di earth?”
All your enemies don open dem mouth wide against you. Dem hiss and gnash dem teeth. Dem talk, “We don swallow her up. Surely dis na di day wey we look for. We don find am. We don see am.”

Di Lord don do wetin e purpose. E don fulfil im word wey e command for di days of old. E don throw down, and no pity. E don cause di enemy to rejoice over you. E don exalt di horn of your adversaries.
Dem heart cry to di Lord. Wall of di daughter of Zion, make tears run down like river day and night. Give yourself no rest. Make di apple of your eye no cease.

Arise, cry out for di night, for di beginning of di watches. Pour out your heart like water before di face of di Lord. Lift up your hands toward am for di life of your young children, wey faint for hunger at di head of every street.
“Look, di Lord, and consider to whom you don do dis! Make women eat dem fruit, di children wey dem dey nurse? Make priest and prophet dey slain for di sanctuary of di Lord?
Di young and di old lie on di ground for di streets. My virgins and my young men don fall by di sword. You don kill dem for di day of your anger. You don slaughter, and no pity.
You don call as for day of solemn assembly my terrors on every side. For di day of di Lord anger no one escape or remain. Dem wey I nurse and bring up, my enemy don consume.”
I be di man wey don see affliction by di rod of im wrath.
E don lead me and make me waka for darkness, and no for light.
Surely against me e dey turn im hand again and again all di day.
E don make my flesh and my skin old. E don break my bones.
E don build against me, and surround me with bitterness and travail.
E don make me dwell for dark places, like dem wey don die long ago.
E don hedge me in, so that I no fit go out. E don make my chain heavy.
Yes, when I cry, and call for help, e shut out my prayer.
E don block my ways with cut stone. E don make my paths crooked.
E be to me like bear lying in wait, like lion for secret places.
E don turn aside my ways, and tear me in pieces. E don make me desolate.
E don bend im bow, and set me as target for di arrow.
E don cause di arrows of im quiver to enter into my heart.
I don become laughingstock to all my people, and dem song all di day.
E don fill me with bitterness. E don make me drunk with wormwood.
E don also break my teeth with gravel stones. E don cover me with ashes.
You don remove my soul far from peace. I forget prosperity.
I talk, “My strength don perish, and my hope from di Lord.”
Remember my affliction and my wandering, di wormwood and di gall.
My soul still remember dem, and dey bowed down inside me.
Dis I recall to my mind. Therefore I hope.
Na through di Lord loving kindnesses say we no dey consumed, because im compassion no fail.
Dem dey new every morning. Great na your faithfulness.
“Di Lord na my portion,” talk my soul. “Therefore I go hope for am.”
Di Lord dey good to dem wey wait for am, to di soul wey seek am.
E dey good say man go hope and wait quietly for di salvation of di Lord.
E dey good for man say e bear di yoke for im youth.
Make am sit alone and keep silent, because e don lay am on am.
Make am put im mouth for di dust, maybe hope go dey.
Make am give im cheek to di one wey strike am. Make am be filled with reproach.
Because di Lord no go cast off forever.
Though e cause grief, yet e go have compassion according to di multitude of im loving kindnesses.
Because e no afflict from im heart, nor grieve di children of men.
To crush under foot all di prisoners of di earth,
to turn aside di right of man before di face of di Most High,
to subvert man for im cause, di Lord no approve.
Who be dis wey talk, and e come to pass, when di Lord no command am?
Out of di mouth of di Most High no evil and good go out?
Why any living man go complain, any man for di punishment of im sins?
Make we search and try our ways, and turn again to di Lord.
Make we lift up our heart with our hands to God for heaven.
We don transgress and don rebel. You no pardon.
You don cover yourself with anger, and pursue us. You don kill, and no pity.
You don cover yourself with cloud, so that no prayer fit pass through.
You don make us di off-scouring and refuse among di peoples.
All our enemies don open dem mouth wide against us.
Fear and di pit don come on us, desolation and destruction.
My eye run down with streams of water, because of di destruction of di daughter of my people.
My eye pour down, and no cease, without any intermission,
until di Lord look down, and see from heaven.
My eye cause grief to my soul, because of all di daughters of my city.
Dem wey be my enemies without cause hunt me down like bird.
Dem don cut off my life for di dungeon, and don cast stone on me.
Waters flow over my head. I talk, “I dey cut off.”
I call on your name, di Lord, out of di lowest dungeon.
You don hear my voice. No hide your ear from my breathing, from my cry.
You draw near for di day wey I call on you. You talk, “No fear.”
Di Lord, you don plead di causes of my soul. You don redeem my life.
Di Lord, you don see my wrong. Judge my cause.
You don see all dem vengeance and all dem plots against me.
You don hear dem reproach, di Lord, and all dem plots against me,
di lips of dem wey rise up against me, and dem murmuring against me all di day.
Behold dem sitting down, and dem rising up. I be dem song.
Render to dem recompense, di Lord, according to di work of dem hands.
Give dem hardness of heart, your curse to dem.
Pursue dem in anger, and destroy dem from under di heavens of di Lord.
How di gold don become dim! How di most pure gold don change! Di stones of di sanctuary dey poured out at di head of every street.
Di precious sons of Zion, wey dey comparable to fine gold, how dem dey regarded as clay pots, di work of di hands of di potter!
Even di jackals offer di breast. Dem nurse dem young ones. Di daughter of my people don become cruel, like di ostriches for di wilderness.
Di tongue of di nursing child cling to di roof of im mouth for thirst. Di young children ask for bread, and no man break am for dem.
Dem wey feed on delicacies dey desolate for di streets. Dem wey dey brought up for scarlet embrace dunghills.
Because di iniquity of di daughter of my people pass di sin of Sodom, wey dem overthrow as for moment, and no hands dey laid on am.
Her princes dey purer pass snow. Dem dey whiter pass milk. Dem dey more ruddy for body pass rubies. Dem polish dey like sapphire.
Now dem visage dey blacker pass soot. Dem no dey recognized for di streets. Dem skin cling to dem bones. E dey withered. E don become like wood.
Dem wey dey killed with di sword dey better pass dem wey dey killed with hunger, because dis ones pine away, stricken through for lack of di fruits of di field.
Di hands of di compassionate women don boil dem own children. Dem become dem food for di destruction of di daughter of my people.
Di Lord don accomplish im wrath. E don pour out im fierce anger. E don kindle fire for Zion, and e don devour im foundations.
Di kings of di earth no believe, neither all di inhabitants of di world, say di adversary and di enemy go enter di gates of Jerusalem.
Na because of di sins of her prophets, and di iniquities of her priests, wey don shed di blood of di righteous for di middle of her.
Dem wander as blind men for di streets. Dem dey polluted with blood, so that men no fit touch dem garments.
“Depart! Unclean!” dem cry to dem. “Depart! Depart! No touch!” So dem flee away and wander. Men talk among di nations, “Dem no go dwell here again.”
Di anger of di Lord don scatter dem. E no go regard dem again. Dem no respect di faces of di priests. Dem no favour di elders.
Our eyes still fail, looking for our vain help. For our watching we don watch for nation wey no fit save.
Dem hunt our steps, so that we no fit waka for our streets. Our end dey near. Our days dey fulfilled, because our end don come.
Our pursuers dey swifter pass di eagles of di sky. Dem pursue us on di mountains. Dem lie in wait for us for di wilderness.
Di breath of our nostrils, di anointed of di Lord, dey taken for dem pits, of whom we talk, “Under im shadow we go live among di nations.”
Rejoice and dey glad, daughter of Edom, wey dwell for di land of Uz. Di cup go pass through to you too. You go dey drunk, and go make yourself naked.
Di punishment of your iniquity don complete, daughter of Zion. E no go carry you away into captivity any more. E go visit your iniquity, daughter of Edom. E go uncover your sins.
Remember, di Lord, wetin don come on us. Look, and see our reproach.
Our inheritance don turn to strangers, our houses to aliens.
We don become orphans and fatherless. Our mothers dey like widows.
We don drink our water for money. Our wood dey sold to us.
Our pursuers dey on our necks. We dey weary, and we get no rest.
We don give di hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to get enough bread.
Our fathers don sin, and dem no dey. We don bear dem iniquities.
Servants rule over us. None dey wey fit deliver us out of dem hand.
We get our bread at di risk of our lives, because of di sword for di wilderness.
Our skin dey black like oven, because of di burning heat of famine.
Dem don ravish di women for Zion, di virgins for di cities of Judah.
Princes dey hanged up by dem hand. Di faces of elders no dey honoured.
Young men carry di millstones, and children stumble under loads of wood.
Di elders don cease from di gate, di young men from dem music.
Di joy of our heart don cease. Our dance don turn to mourning.
Di crown don fall from our head. Woe to us, because we don sin!
For dis our heart dey faint. For dis things our eyes dey dim:
for di mountain of Zion, wey dey desolate. Di foxes waka on am.
You, di Lord, reign forever. Your throne dey from generation to generation.
Why you forget us forever, and forsake us so long?
Turn us to you, di Lord, and we go dey turned. Renew our days as of old.
But you don utterly reject us. You dey very angry against us.
